record.paper_title: Results and Open Problems in Mathematical General Relativity
record.original_question: For vacuum Einstein spacetimes whose spatial manifold is S^3, must the spacetime collapse in the future?

evidence.quote: It is conjectured, and proved for spaces with spatial isometry group, that spacetimes with spacemanifold S3 collapse in the future.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, g)$ be a globally hyperbolic vacuum spacetime, i.e., a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold satisfying the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$, admitting a Cauchy surface diffeomorphic to the 3-sphere $S^3$. Consider the cosmologically normalized (CMC) Einstein flow on $S^3$, parametrized by mean curvature $\tau$ of CMC Cauchy slices $\Sigma_\tau$, and let $h(\tau)$ denote the induced Riemannian metric on $\Sigma_\tau$.

Prove or disprove: every such maximal future Cauchy development collapses in the future in the sense of Cheeger–Gromov, i.e., as $\tau$ tends to its supremum (corresponding to future infinity in the CMC time gauge), the volume-normalized geometry $(\Sigma_\tau, h(\tau))$ collapses with bounded curvature — equivalently, the injectivity radius (after appropriate rescaling so that sectional curvatures remain bounded) tends to zero uniformly on $\Sigma_\tau$.

(The analogous statement is known to hold under the additional assumption that the spacetime admits a continuous spatial isometry group acting on the $S^3$ Cauchy surfaces.)
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that vacuum Einstein flows on Cauchy surfaces with non-hyperbolizable topology (such as $S^3$) exhibit future collapse is part of an active research program linking Einstein flow to Thurston geometrization. Results exist under symmetry assumptions and in related collapse-with-bounded-curvature settings, but the general $S^3$ case appears to remain open as of recent work.

status_evidence.title: Collapsing in the Einstein Flow
status_evidence.snippet: For certain manifold topologies, the Einstein flow converges to a hyperbolic metric, whereas in the non-hyperbolic cases the Einstein flow collapses the 3-manifold along circular fibers or embedded tori, with bounded curvature.
status_evidence.claim: Collapse of the Einstein flow on non-hyperbolizable 3-manifolds is an active topic, with results in restricted settings.

status_evidence.title: Hamiltonian reduction, the Einstein flow, and collapse of 3-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Reduced Einstein flow and conformal volume collapse for 3-manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: The collapse conjecture for spaces like $S^3$ is formulated within the reduced Einstein flow framework.

status_evidence.title: A large data result for vacuum Einstein's equations
status_evidence.snippet: Recent large-data results address future asymptotic behavior of vacuum Einstein flow on closed 3-manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: The general future asymptotic behavior on $S^3$ has not been resolved; research continues.
